Definition: {to denude (especially in a disgraceful sense); by implication, to exile (captives being usually stripped); figuratively, to reveal}
BiblicalUsage: gᵉlâh — to reveal. That is the whole of it, and it is enough: 8 occurrences, and in Ezra and Daniel the meaning never wavers. I keep coming back to the simple reading because the simple reading is the true one.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe gᵉlâh matters because God reveals what is hidden, and He brings His people home. I hold that the simple reading is the true one, and I will not trade it for a clever one.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
